key_facts: On July 17, 2024, Plaintiff completed an online employment application with Federal Express Corporation ('FedEx') for a position in FedEx's delivery and package handling operations in California, confirmed by an automated email from 'Olivia from FedEx' (fedex@paradox.ai). As part of its standard pre-employment screening, FedEx — through a human-resources function identified as 'FEDEX GROUND HR' — initiated a background check through First Advantage (fadv.com). On March 10, 2025 at 1:44 PM, Plaintiff received a 'FedEx Pre-Adverse Employment Action Notice' from First Advantage (DoNotReply@fadv.com) directing him to review the pre-adverse action notification via a secure portal link. A duplicate pre-adverse notice bearing the same subject line was sent the next day, March 11, 2025 at 7:48 AM, to a second email address associated with Plaintiff (bnn.cdl@gmail.com) with a distinct portal key, followed by five further reminder notices dated March 11 (1:45 PM), March 12, March 13, March 14, and March 16, 2025 — an unusually persistent notice cadence. On March 19, 2025 at 1:47 PM — nine days after the original pre-adverse notice — Plaintiff received a 'FedEx Adverse Employment Action Notice' from First Advantage confirming FedEx had taken final adverse action, definitively denying him employment. FedEx provided no written communication identifying any basis for the denial other than the background screening report; no other disqualifying information existed in Plaintiff's application. Plaintiff is a registrant on California's Megan's Law sex offender registry, and alleges on information and belief that the First Advantage report disclosed that status to FedEx (together with a statutory disclaimer warning that the information could not lawfully be used for employment purposes) and that FedEx used it as the basis for the denial, in violation of Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E).

Complaint for Damages filed July 15, 2026, San Joaquin Superior Court, file-stamped by Clerk Stephanie Bohrer (Deputy Mia Stipe). Assigned STK-CV-UWT-2026-0009118, Dept. 10B, Hon. Blanca Banuelos; CMC January 14, 2027, 8:45 AM; service deadline September 13, 2026 (60 days, CRC 3.110). Case assignment notice issued July 15, 2026 by Deputy Clerk Mia Stipe. Unlike Matter 22 (Pilot) and Matter 23 (Macy's), Plaintiff does not possess a copy of the underlying First Advantage background report — the secure portal link expired before he could preserve it — so the pleading relies on information-and-belief allegations regarding the report's contents and FedEx's use of the registry information, corroborated by the paper trail of application confirmation, two pre-adverse notices, five reminders, and the final adverse-action notice. A complete, ready-to-serve filing packet has been assembled combining the court-stamped Complaint page 1, the plain (unstamped) Complaint pages 2-16, the signed/verified Complaint pages 17-18 (jury demand and verification, both bearing Plaintiff's original signature), the filed SUM-100 Summons (court-stamped July 15, 2026, Clerk Stephanie Bohrer/Deputy Mia Stipe, Case No. STK-CV-UWT-2026-0009118), and the Notice of Case Assignment and Notice of Hearing, in that order — Summons, Complaint (stamped p.1 through signed pp.17-18), Notice. On July 21, 2026, a SER-001 Request for Sheriff to Serve Court Papers was completed and electronically signed, directing the Los Angeles County Sheriff to serve FedEx's California registered agent — C T Corporation System (Amanda Garcia), 330 N Brand Blvd, Ste 700, Glendale, CA 91203 — with the Summons, Complaint, and Notice of Case Assignment; the form also lists the January 14, 2027 CMC date and the September 13, 2026 service deadline (CRC 3.110). The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department Filing Receipt (printed July 21, 2026, File No. 2026075280) confirms the request was accepted — Service Type: Summons & Complaint (SC); Waiver: Waiver-FW — confirming the FW-003 fee waiver extends to the Sheriff's service fee. Per the LA County Sheriff's Civil File Status printed July 25, 2026 (Case Manager P. M Brown; case Active as of 07/21/2026), the Summons & Complaint was SERVED July 24, 2026 at 9:00 AM (1 attempt) on Federal Express Corporation, accepted by Ct Corporation System, Agent for Service, through Jaqueline Mejia, a California Authorized Employee, per CCP § 416.10; the sheriff's fee remained waived. Proof of service will be filed with the court well ahead of the September 13, 2026 CRC 3.110 deadline. COMPUTED DEADLINES FROM THE JULY 24, 2026 SERVICE DATE: responsive pleading (answer or demurrer) due August 24, 2026 — 30 days from service under CCP §412.20(a)(3); the raw 30-day count lands on Sunday, August 23, 2026, which CCP §12a rolls forward to the next court day, Monday, August 24. If FedEx elects to demur rather than answer, CCP §430.41(a)(2) requires the parties to meet and confer in person or by telephone at least 5 days before that responsive-pleading date — i.e., by August 19, 2026 — before any demurrer can be filed; if FedEx cannot complete that meet-and-confer in time, its counsel must instead file and serve a declaration by August 24, 2026 explaining the good-faith attempt, which triggers an automatic 30-day extension. As of this writing, no answer, demurrer, or meet-and-confer outreach has been received from FedEx. NOTED FOR AWARENESS: this matter and Matter 26 were filed the same day (July 15, 2026) in the same courthouse (San Joaquin Sup. Ct.), assigned to adjacent departments, asserting the identical PC §290.46(j) theory — but against different corporate defendants arising from separate hiring transactions, so a CRC 3.300 notice of related case is unlikely to be required (that rule keys on common questions of fact/law arising from the same or related transactions, not merely the same legal theory). No such notice has been filed either way; flagged here only so the point isn't overlooked if either court raises it sua sponte.
damages: Statutory civil remedy under PC § 290.46(j)(4)(A): actual damages or $25,000, whichever is greater, plus attorney fees, for each unlawful use of registry information. CONSERVATIVE: ~$40,000 (statutory minimum plus modest emotional distress; no wage documentation on file to support a large lost-wages claim, since Plaintiff never began working for FedEx). MODERATE: ~$95,000 (statutory penalty, ICRAA punitive damages up to $5,000 for willful noncompliance, emotional distress, and partial fee-shifting). AGGRESSIVE: ~$220,000 (treble-adjacent aggregation across all six causes of action plus Civil Code § 3294 punitive damages, if discovery yields the actual First Advantage report and confirms willful registry-based denial). Note: because Plaintiff was never hired, there are no lost W-2 wages comparable to Matter 22 — the primary economic recovery theory is the PC § 290.46(j)(4)(A) statutory penalty and lost opportunity/career-advancement damages, not back pay from an existing job.
risk: Favorable on the law (PC § 290.46(j)(2)(E) is a categorical, exception-free prohibition and negligence per se under Evid. Code § 669) but evidentiarily thinner than Matters 22/23: FedEx never issued a written admission comparable to Pilot's Post-Adverse Action Notice or Macy's' HireRight internal comments naming the registry as the basis for denial. The First Advantage notices establish the timeline (application → pre-adverse notice → 9-day gap → final adverse action) and FedEx's general practice of background screening through a vendor known to include statutory registry disclaimers, but the complaint pleads FedEx's actual use of registry information 'on information and belief' throughout. Discovery (a subpoena to First Advantage for the underlying report, or FedEx's hiring file) would be needed to convert this from a plausible to a proven claim. The five reminder notices sent to two different email addresses is useful circumstantial evidence that Plaintiff was a live, monitored applicant in FedEx's system at the time of denial.
